segments.title: Marching to the Sound of the Guns
segments.narrative_purpose: Show Grouchy intercepting the Prussians at the Lasne bridges and Napoleon launching the Old Guard.
segments.why_a_scene: Shows the high-stakes dawn confrontation at La Belle Alliance where Marshal Ney presses Napoleon to unleash the grand battery and heavy cuirassiers immediately while the chalk ground is dry.

scene.place: La Belle Alliance forward command ridge
scene.want: Open the grand battery and launch the cuirassiers at 6:00 AM while the ground is firm
scene.obstacle_want: Hold the reserve cavalry until Wellington exposes his center
scene.turn: Napoleon sees Wellington center unreinforced and orders Ney to sound the general charge
scene.exit: Ney spurs his horse down the ridge to lead the heavy cuirassiers
scene.surface_topic: Whether the frost-hardened chalk can support an immediate dawn assault
scene.real_subject: Gambling the entire French Empire on a four-hour window before Prussia arrives

audio_lines.text: What if Napoleon marched at dawn?
June eighteenth, eighteen fifteen: sodden black mud traps seventy-two thousand French troops south of Mont-Saint-Jean while artillery caissons sink axle-deep.
One downpour rewrote European history, forcing the Emperor to delay his grand battery barrage for four fatal hours while Prussian columns closed in from Wavre.
Disciplined British squares lock bayonets in silence along the reverse slope.
In our counterfactual divergence, frost-hardened chalk soil holds firm beneath the French cannon wheels at six in the morning before a single Prussian scout crosses the Lasne valley.
Eighty brass twelve-pounders roar at once.
Dense columns of dark-blue infantry surge past the orchard walls of Hougoumont, driving Wellington's forward riflemen back toward the sunken ridge in swirling cannon smoke.
The chalk beneath the wheels is firm, Sire! Let the batteries open now before their center locks the ridge!
Their center wavers, Marshal. Unleash the heavy cuirassiers now!
Sound the general charge—we break Mont-Saint-Jean before Bülow reaches the woods!
Ney's heavy cuirassiers thunder up the unscathed slope three hours ahead of schedule, shattering the allied center before a single Prussian brigade can emerge from the eastern woods.
By noon, Brussels falls—yet can a bankrupt Paris sustain an empire reborn in blood?
